questions.stem: Which system is described as the 'treasure map' that holds each device's location, warranty status, and user history but not the physical equipment itself?

choices.text: Configuration management database (CMDB)
Service level agreement (SLA)
Standard operating procedure (SOP)
Incident report

questions.explanation: The CMDB is the asset-tracking database - it stores coordinates, warranty status, and user history for every device without holding the equipment itself.
questions.trap: An SLA is a service contract defining expectations, not an inventory of assets.

questions.stem: How do asset tags link a physical device to its record in the asset database?

choices.text: They encrypt the device's hard drive
Stickers with barcodes you scan to pull up the device's history
They assign the device a static IP address
They are SLA contracts attached to the device

questions.explanation: Asset tags are barcode stickers; scanning one instantly brings up that device's record in the CMDB.
questions.trap: Asset tags are about identification and tracking, not encryption or network addressing.

questions.stem: What is the correct order of the procurement life cycle described in the review?

choices.text: Invoice, then request, then purchase order, then payment
Purchase order, then request, then payment, then invoice
Request, then purchase order (PO), then invoice, then accounting releases funds
Payment, then invoice, then request, then purchase order

questions.explanation: The procurement gates run: request, then PO (negotiate the deal), then invoice (vendor asks for payment), then accounting releases the funds.
questions.trap: The invoice comes after the PO, not first; the vendor only invoices once an order is placed.

questions.stem: In a ticketing system, what determines the priority of a ticket?

choices.text: The alphabetical order of the user's name
The time of day the ticket was opened
Whichever ticket has the longest description
The severity level (a broken mouse is low; a server down is critical)

questions.explanation: Severity dictates priority. A broken mouse is low severity; a downed server is critical and jumps the queue.
questions.trap: Priority is risk/impact-based (severity), not first-come or based on description length.

questions.stem: A tier-one technician receives a ticket that is too complex for their team. What is the correct action?

choices.text: Escalate it to a specialized team such as networking
Close the ticket as unsolvable
Delete the ticket to keep the queue clean
Reassign it to the end user to handle

questions.explanation: When a ticket exceeds tier-one's ability, you escalate - hand it off to a specialized team like networking.
questions.trap: Closing or deleting a ticket you can't solve hides the problem instead of routing it to the right experts.

questions.stem: Which document is compared to a 'cooking recipe' that ensures every technician produces a consistent result on routine tasks?

choices.text: Incident report
Standard operating procedure (SOP)
Service level agreement (SLA)
Purchase order (PO)

questions.explanation: An SOP is the recipe for routine tasks; if every tech follows it, the outcome is consistent every time.
questions.trap: An incident report documents something that went wrong; it is not the recipe for routine work.

questions.stem: After a security breach or workplace accident, which document is filed to create a legal history of the event?

choices.text: A standard operating procedure
A purchase order
An incident report
An asset tag

questions.explanation: When things go wrong (a breach or accident), you file an incident report to create a legal history of the event.
questions.trap: SOPs are for routine repeatable tasks; the record of an adverse event is an incident report.

questions.stem: Why is the offboarding checklist called an 'exam favorite,' and what critical step does it enforce?

choices.text: It assigns the new hire a desk and badge
It orders replacement hardware through procurement
It schedules the annual security audit
It ensures data is decrypted and backed up before the device is wiped

questions.explanation: Offboarding must follow the checklist so data is decrypted and backed up BEFORE wiping the device - otherwise the data is lost forever.
questions.trap: Assigning a desk and badge is onboarding; offboarding is about safely recovering data and revoking access.

questions.stem: An SLA guarantees a vendor will fix an outage within 4 hours or face financial penalties. What is an SLA?

choices.text: A contract that defines service expectations between parties
A barcode sticker for tracking equipment
A database of all configuration items
A step-by-step recipe for routine tasks

questions.explanation: A service level agreement is a contract defining expectations - such as a guaranteed repair window backed by penalties.
questions.trap: The asset database is the CMDB and the routine recipe is the SOP; the SLA is specifically the service contract.

questions.stem: Why does the review stress documenting the resolution clearly in a ticket?

choices.text: To increase the ticket's severity level
So the next technician doesn't have to reinvent the wheel
To bypass the change-management process
To automatically issue a purchase order

questions.explanation: Clear resolution notes let the next technician reuse the fix instead of solving the same problem from scratch.
questions.trap: Documentation is about knowledge transfer, not about changing severity or skipping process.
